newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission wary in China/Denmark rights row.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission wary in China/Denmark rights row.

text.p: The European Commission trod warily into the human rights row between China and Denmark on Tuesday, backing a U.N. resolution criticising China while playing down the effects of EU divisions on the issue.
"Our policy towards China, especially (in terms of) human rights, will remain the same," Commission spokesman Peter Guilford told a news conference.
He was replying to reporters' questions about warnings from Beijing that Denmark would suffer a political and trade backlash if it raised a U.N. resolution criticising China's human rights record.

"We don't exactly know what those threats mean. If the threats imply trade, trade policy is a common European policy in which, of course, Community countries show solidarity and negotiate together," he said.
Guilford said the Commission still backed the resolution, despite opposition within the EU from France, among others, which wants behind-the-scenes dialogue instead.
"It's not a perfect way but it's one useful way of impressing on the Chinese our European opinion ...We have never claimed it would sort out Chinese human rights overnight," Guilford said.

Denmark is to table a text later this week at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva after thwarted attempts to agree a joint EU motion, an outcome Guilford said would not undermine the credibility of future efforts by EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan to raise human rights issues with Bejing.
"I think he has as much credibility as he did before. I cannot see that credibility should be necessarily diminished in any way," he said.
